2607.25953.title: Polistemics: Evaluating LLMs as Information Mediators in Politics & Elections
2607.25953.paper_summary: As LLMs increasingly mediate the political information citizens rely on, there is still no standardized way to assess whether they do so responsibly. We introduce Polistemics, a theory-grounded benchmark for evaluating LLMs as mediators of political information in elections. Prior work has treated this task as reproduction rather than mediation, leaving its epistemic dimensions and interaction with imperfect information unaddressed. We ground the evaluation in Epistemic Modesty, a normative standard derived from citizens' epistemic agency, and test it across controlled settings that vary informational properties such as clarity, noise, and consistency. Applying the benchmark to three state-of-the-art LLMs on the 2025 German and Dutch elections, we find that high aggregate scores mask systematic failures. Models mediate reliably under clear evidence but break down under absent, vague, or contradictory information, while flattening the intensity of political language. These failures are likely driven by party priors, influenced by party labels and output language. Reliable mediation appears achievable, but no model delivers it consistently.
2607.25953.paper_summary_zh: 隨著大型語言模型（LLMs）越來越多地介入公民所依賴的政治資訊，目前仍然沒有標準化的方法來評估它們是否負責任地進行這一介入。我們引入了Polistemics，一個基於理論的基準，用於評估LLMs在選舉中作為政治資訊的介入者。先前的研究將這一任務視為再現而非介入，未能解決其認識論維度及與不完美資訊的互動。我們將評估基於認識論謙遜，這是一個源自公民認識論能動性的規範標準，並在控制環境中測試，這些環境變化了資訊特性，如清晰度、噪音和一致性。我們將該基準應用於三個最先進的LLMs，針對2025年德國和荷蘭選舉進行測試，發現高整體分數掩蓋了系統性失敗。在清晰證據下，模型能可靠地進行介入，但在缺失、模糊或矛盾的資訊下則失效，同時降低了政治語言的強度。這些失敗可能是由於政黨先驗所驅動，受到政黨標籤和輸出語言的影響。可靠的介入似乎是可實現的，但沒有任何模型能持續提供這一結果。
2607.25953.author: Baran Peters et.al.
